issues.description: The solution defines assembleBookstore with a parameter (private static func assembleBookstore(count: Int) -> Bookstore) but main() calls assembleBookstore() with no arguments. The template's commented stub also shows assembleBookstore() with no parameters and the problem statement describes assembling the Bookstore without specifying a parameter. This parameter mismatch will cause a compile error or confusion for students about the required signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the assembleBookstore signature consistent across artifacts. Preferably remove the unused parameter from the solution and declare: private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore { ... } so main() can call assembleBookstore() as shown, and the template, problem statement, and solution match. Alternatively, if a parameter is intended, update the template and main() call to pass the parameter and document the parameter in the problem statement.

issues.description: The function assembleBookstore is described in the problem statement and appears in the template as a parameterless function (assembleBookstore()), but the solution implements assembleBookstore with a parameter (assembleBookstore(count: Int)). This introduces a signature/identifier mismatch for the same conceptual entity (the bookstore assembly routine) and can confuse students about which function to implement/call.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the function signature across artifacts. Either remove the unused parameter from the solution and implement private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore, or update the problem statement and template to require assembleBookstore(count: Int). Preferred fix: change the solution to implement assembleBookstore() without parameters so it matches the problem description and template.
